defs.def: feeling tired and impatient because you have lost interest in sb/sth or because you have nothing to do （对某人/事物）厌倦的；烦闷的

ex.s: Sure, my friends and I loved to _____46_____ about how bored we were in the middle of nowhere; _____47_____ , as I finish up my junior year of college, I’m convinced that it took _____48_____ our small town to realize how much we actually loved it and what exactly we loved about it.
ex.t: 当然，我和朋友们过去总爱____，抱怨我们在这偏僻地方有多无聊；____，当我大学三年级即将结束时，我确信，正是____我们的小镇，才让我们意识到自己其实有多爱它，以及我们究竟爱它什么。

ex.s: Even the most engaged and committed audience will eventually get bored.
ex.t: 骑行是最经济、最可持续、最有趣的探索这座城市的方式，这里有美丽的运河、公园、广场和无数的灯光。
伊桑为什么担心父母独自生活？

ex.s: I spent much of the time when I was there feeling frightened and more than a little bored!
ex.t: 我在那里的那段时光，大多感到害怕，而且远不止一点点无聊！

ex.s: After a while, she discovered that surfing the Internet could help her feel less lonely and bored.
ex.t: 一段时间后，她发现上网能让她少些孤独和无聊。

ex.s: Christiane Heinicke, one of the people who lived there, said that one of the biggest issues was feeling bored.
ex.t: 曾住在那里的克里斯蒂安·海尼克说，最大的问题之一就是感到无聊。

ex.s: So if a student has his head lowered to look at his watch, it implies he is bored and just counting the minutes for the class to end.
ex.t: 所以如果一个学生低头看表，就表明他感到无聊，只是在数着分钟等下课。

ex.s: While it is easy to perceive when students are interested, bored, or distracted, it is sometimes much harder to distinguish when students are troubled.
ex.t: 虽然学生何时感兴趣、无聊或分心很容易察觉，但有时要分辨学生何时烦恼则困难得多。
